calls.body: The Mammoth are one of the league’s best for shot volume, but the Lightning are one of the best at keeping shots away. We’ll side with the Mammoth.

surprises.head: Tampa Bay’s power play was at its best
surprises.body: Tampa Bay’s power play has been near the top of the league for years. Even by those standards, this was a big night: 15.4 expected goals per 60 on the power play, against their usual 7.5 and a league average of 7.6. A team strays this far about once every 25 games.

surprises.head: Utah shortened their bench
surprises.body: Utah leans on their bottom six more than most teams. Not tonight: the bottom six played 39% of the forwards’ 5-on-5 time, against their usual 45% and a league average of 42%. A team strays this far about once every 45 games.

story.head: Kucherov sets the Lightning’s points record
paras: There were five goals in the first period alone. Jake Guentzel got the scoring started for the Lightning early in the period, but Kailer Yamamoto made it 1-1 for Utah just under two minutes later. Pontus Holmberg and Brayden Point scored less than three minutes apart midway through the period to put the Bolts up 3-1. Dylan Guenther cut Tampa Bay’s lead to 3-2 on the power play just under five minutes later. Conor Geekie made it 4-2 for the Lightning early in the second, but Anders Lee made it 4-3 midway through the period. The Lightning’s Zemgus Girgensons left late in the period and didn’t return. The next day, he was listed as day to day. Dmitri Simashev, in his 40th NHL game, scored his first NHL goal, set up by Andrew Peeke, later in the period to tie it 4-4. Simashev scored his second NHL goal less than two minutes into overtime to win it.

Nothing much separated these two on the chances. This one could have gone either way. Karel Vejmelka made 29 saves for the Mammoth, and Dennis Hildeby allowed five goals on 28 shots. The Mammoth moved to 8-4-0, still first in the Central, while the Lightning fell to 7-3-1, slipping to fourth in the Atlantic.

items.text: Nikita Kucherov passed Steven Stamkos to become the Lightning’s all-time leader in points, with 1,138.
NHL.com had projected the Lightning with 11 forwards and seven defensemen, but they dressed 12 and six.
One of the preview’s two calls held.
